key_insight: An exponentially weighted ensemble of five deep learning models improved lung adenocarcinoma histologic growth pattern classification on H&E slides by using model-specific QWK scores to set ensemble weights.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help support more accurate digital pathology grading, which may improve prognosis assessment and treatment planning in lung adenocarcinoma.
method: 25,545 image patches from Dartmouth-Hitchcock whole-slide H&E images at 40x magnification
Compared EfficientNet-B3, DeiT3, Swin Transformer, Vision Transformer, and ConvNeXt
Used stratified 5-fold cross-validation with softmax-weighted ensemble aggregation based on per-model QWK
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved 96.52% accuracy and kappa = 0.9648, outperforming the best individual model by +0.0087 kappa with significant McNemar and bootstrap results.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on a single dataset and patch-level workflow, so external validation across institutions and slide-level clinical deployment are still needed.
paper_title: Exponentially weighted ensemble deep learning for histologic growth pattern classification in lung adenocarcinoma
